title: M08.13 the act tool as a draw-down client · M08.14 the headless posture

check:standing-consumer-loop.fixture: real wallet.network principal-authority fixture, Solo ordering profile
act_tool_clauses: PASS M08.13: the act tool's advertised filters ARE the daemon's lease projection — operations, tools, metered unit, usages, budget and expiry rendered from the connector record, with the capability handle and an explicit host_config_is_authority=false — 200 {"allowed_tools":["ping"],"expires_at_ms":
PASS M08.13: an interactive act completes WITHOUT a per-call signature — it draws against the caller's standing lease and the daemon records the draw — 200 · 1 draw receipt(s)

PASS MUTATION DRILL (M08.13): widening the HOST config's filters beyond the lease changes nothing the daemon enforces — the act still refuses at the lease bound (tool outside the template) and the answer says the host filters were ignored — 403/standing_envelope_tool_outside_template host_filters_ig

PASS M08.14: a HEADLESS act presenting only the out-of-band capability handle draws under the same lease — no product session and no per-call signature; the caller's own identity is still resolved, because a handle selects a lease and never becomes a principal — 200 · 1 headless draw receipt(s)

PASS M08.14: the interactive and headless draws produce receipt chains that are byte-identical except their subject identity — same kind, same field set, same envelope and grant, same posture, both admitted through the same intent family — true · silent_within_policy/silent_within_policy
PASS M08.14: an act with NO lease authority — no session, no handle — refuses typed and never falls back to the host's configuration — 403/act_no_authority
PASS a capability handle that names no active lease refuses — the handle SELECTS a lease, it never authorizes one — 403/act_capability_handle_unknown
PASS the act tool draws down the SAME envelope as every other path: the third draw exhausts the 3-usage lease and the fourth refuses at the bound — 200 then 403/max_usages

what_changed: daemon: GET /v1/model-mount/mcp/act/tools renders the act tool per connection from the connector record's standing lease (a read projection); POST /v1/model-mount/mcp/act delegates to the connector-invoke draw-down gate and states that host filters were ignored.

daemon: the connector-invoke gate accepts an OPAQUE CAPABILITY HANDLE as the acting subject beside a session_ref (never both); the handle must name the connection's active lease exactly, receipts are written under a handle-derived subject, and the acting subject is folded into the request facets so a session's grant cannot replay as a handle act.
daemon: both act routes are classified in the MCP route census, which fails daemon readiness closed on an unclassified MCP route — it caught these two before they could serve.
findings: A headless act is NOT anonymous: the caller's identity is still resolved by the daemon, and the handle only selects the lease. The first cut modelled headless as cookie-less and was refused 401 by the session gate, correctly.

The act route minted a session record for headless draws in its first cut; that was a second authority story about the same draw and was removed — the handle crosses to the one gate as it was presented.
